# Volume versus surface certificates: cone reweighting has an exact defect

This note retains the corrected signs in `candidate 7127f9c7b67df7cb`. It does not identify independent couplings. Its new interface is an explicit cone conversion of the energy-source and original-volume marginals, together with the exact defect that prevents converting a boundary martingale into a volume martingale by that weighting.

## 1. A centered projective cone law

Let K be a positive convex d-body, y interior, N=d+1, and let L(X)=1+a·(X-y) be the optimal positive projective denominator. Put E=integral_K L^(-N). The optimality identity is

    integral_K (X-y)L^(-N-1)=0,
    integral_K L^(-N-1)=E.

At almost every boundary point let n be the outward unit normal and h_y=n·(X-y)>0. Gauss–Green, valid for arbitrary convex bodies and the smooth bounded kernels, gives

    integral_boundary h_y L^(-N)=d E,
    integral_boundary (X-y) h_y L^(-N)=0.                (1)

For the first identity, the divergence is d L^(-N)-N a·(X-y)L^(-N-1). For the second it is N(X-y)L^(-N)-N(X-y)a·(X-y)L^(-N-1)=N(X-y)L^(-N-1).

Thus h_y L^(-N)dS/(dE) is a genuine probability measure with barycenter y. Similarly h_g dS/(dV), with g the ordinary centroid, has barycenter g. These identities include d=1 with endpoint counting measure.

Now take the regular SAME-eta unpenalized certificate, with proper response coefficients eta_i delta_i, Delta their sum, and multiplier ell. The source and target of its base-volume martingale are

    mu=sum_i eta_i delta_i/ell_(p_i) delta_(p_i),
    nu=Delta sum_z V_z/(M ell_z) delta_z.

Their exact boundary-cone lifts are

    mu^E=sum_i [eta_i delta_i/ell_(p_i)]
                   h_(y_i)L_i^(-N)dS_(K_pi)/(d E_i),
    nu^V=sum_z [Delta V_z/(M ell_z)]
                   h_(g_z)dS_(K_z)/(d V_z).             (2)

They have the desired base marginals, but their continuous first-moment difference is EXACTLY

    integral X d(nu^V-mu^E)
       =Delta/M sum_z V_z g_z/ell_z
                    -sum_i eta_i delta_i y_i/ell_(p_i). (3)

Base convex order does not set (3) to zero. In particular the centered source cone law does not repair the previously disproved uniform-fiber lift: the ordinary target cone law has the SAME conditional means as the uniform target fibers.

## 2. Why reweighting a surface martingale is not a solution

Suppose a physical surface martingale preserves the continuous normal n, and a row is labeled by an actual common support plane

    a·z+n·X=b.

Such bounded Borel labels and conditional rows are available in the audited arbitrary-body extension; no polyhedral minimizer is required. Write w'=(z',X'), w=(z,X), and delta w=w'-w. Choose interior centers c_z and define r(w)=n·(X-c_z)>0 on the corresponding fiber boundary.

Contact and the row barycenter identity give the exact equations

    E[r(w')]-r(w)=-n·(E[c_z']-c_z),                    (4)
    E[r(w') delta w]
       =-E[delta w (a·(z'-z)+n·(c_z'-c_z))].           (5)

Thus target cone weighting can change the row MASS when the center graph is nonaffine. Even when c_z=A z+c_0 is affine, (4) vanishes but (5) is

    -Q_row (a+A^T n,0),
    Q_row=E[delta w delta w^T]>=0.                      (6)

The weighted row is a martingale precisely when this vector vanishes. Equivalently the variance of (a+A^T n)·(z'-z) is zero, so r is constant along that row. This is the exact condition; normal preservation and affine centers alone do not suffice.

The covariance sign in (6) agrees with the corrected negative base-covariance sign in the archived mixed-flux formula. The present observation is its measure-conversion interpretation, not a second proof that mixed covariance vanishes. The inverse-ell factor in (2) introduces further weighting and cannot remove these terms merely from the separate base martingale's ell tightness.

## 3. Exact fiber force of the buffered physical density

Assume a regular fixed covering menu, allowing additional atomic rows, and use covariance-normalized continuous cap normals Gamma(u_ij)=1. Let S_ij(z) be the actual proper coarea in fiber z, zero on strict full/empty fibers, with total S_ij. Let theta_ij=(rho_ij/S_ij)/B_i, delta_i=epsilon f_i/B_i, and sum_j rho_ij u_ij=epsilon f_i a_i. Let Xi be the unpenalized common physical density, including the original-volume normalization terms and -Delta log ell_z/(NM).

Its fiberwise normal flux is exactly

    F_z:=integral_boundary(K_z) Xi_z n
       =sum_(i,j) eta_i theta_ij S_ij(z)u_ij
                    -sum_(i:p_i=z) eta_i delta_i a_i.   (7)

Indeed a regular cap indicator contributes S_ij(z)u_ij by the cap divergence theorem. An energy kernel contributes -eta_i delta_i a_i by its optimality identities. The centered quadratic contributes zero because integral_K(X-g_z)=0. All fiberwise constants, including atomic selectors and log ell, have zero normal flux. No facet allocation is silently used at a supporting cap: this displayed linear formula is restricted to regular rows.

Section base centroids and the buffered normal balance give

    sum_z F_z=0,    sum_z z tensor F_z=0.                (8)

They do not force F_z=0 pointwise. For ordinary-centroid radial speeds h_z=n·(X-g_z), the exact remaining torque is

    sum_z integral_boundary(K_z) Xi_z h_z
                           =-sum_z g_z·F_z.             (9)

One may prove (9) from the null common dilation and (7), or directly by divergence. In the direct calculation the cap cut term is

    sum_i eta_i delta_i[a_i·(y_i-g_pi)-1]
                                         -sum_z g_z·F_z.

The energy kernels contribute sum_i eta_i delta_i[d/N-a_i·(y_i-g_pi)]. The centered quadratic contributes (d+2)Delta/2. The constant correction contributes -d(N+2)Delta/(2N), and geometric normalization makes the log term zero. Together these scalar terms cancel exactly. This records the nonaffine centroid torque instead of discarding it as a consequence of base balance.

## 4. Actual parameter-optimal interval calibration

Use K_-=K_+=[-1,1], K_0=[-1,2], ell=1 and the actual small positive invariant buffer. The unique middle mark is y=1/4+delta/2, where 0<delta<1/100, and

    E=(35+4delta-4delta^2)/12,
    a=4(1-2delta)/(35+4delta-4delta^2).

Choose the actual upper critical cap and either of the regular isolated lower critical caps from the audited all-slope calculation. Their upper/lower coareas are 3 sqrt(Sigma) and sqrt(Sigma). The exact buffered balance gives

    rho_upper=(1+delta a)/2,
    rho_lower=(1-delta a)/2,
    theta_upper=(1+delta a)/[2(2-delta a)],
    Delta=3delta/(2-delta a).

Formula (7) yields

    F_-=F_+=theta_upper,    F_0=-2theta_upper.

Since the ordinary centroid graph is (0,1/2,0),

    sum_z g_z F_z=-theta_upper !=0,
    sum_z integral Xi_z h_(g_z)=theta_upper>0.           (10)

Nevertheless this SAME single-group parameter certificate has the exact volume martingale delta_0 to (2,3,2)/7 and is the unique optimum over all normalized concave arrays. Formula (3) here is

    Delta(3/14-y)=-Delta(1/28+delta/2)<0.                (11)

This is NOT a joint body minimum or a claimed physical surface convex-order certificate. It shows exactly that full parameter convex order and genuine cap/section criticality do not cancel either defect. The formal centroid-centered erosion in (10) is in fact incompatible: shrinking the endpoints by r and the middle about 1/2 by r would require 1/2-3r/2<=-r, hence r>=1. Its positive formal response therefore cannot be promoted to an actual descent.

## 5. Conclusion within the stated scope

At a genuine regular joint minimum both certificates exist, but the conversion between them must still control (3)–(6), not simply cone-weight a surface coupling. The finite parameter martingale provides all convex base tests and ell-tight source relations; it alone does not sign or eliminate the actual nonaffine centroid torque in (9). A use of joint body minimality beyond the already written certificates remains necessary to remove that obstruction.
